verdict.rationale: Clerk's pricing page lists passkeys as an authentication method, and its site documents built-in email and SMS one-time passcodes, so passkeys and email OTP exist as Clerk sign-in capabilities. Coverage is incomplete: passkeys are restricted to Pro and higher plans, and the changelog also describes passkeys as an MFA second factor. Missing for 10: any evidence of magic-link sign-in, in-depth first-party docs on configuring passkeys and OTP as primary sign-in methods, passkey availability on the Free plan, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can offer passkeys/WebAuthn and passwordless options like magic links or email OTP as first-class sign-in methods

citations.quote: Passkeys — Authenticate with any form of passkeys
Email and SMS one-time passcodes — Fast and reliable one-time passcode delivery with built-in brute force prevention.
Users can now use a passkey as their second factor for multi-factor authentication after they sign in another way.
